title: Eurostat SDG_11_52 – Premature deaths due to exposure to PM2.5 (Italy)
summary: Eurostat SDG indicator 11_52: annual number and rate of premature deaths attributable to long-term exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) for Italy. Covers 18 data years from 2005 to 2023 (with a gap in 2006). The data is national-level (Italy only), annual grain, and is sourced from ESTAT (Eurostat). Provides two measures: count (NR) and rate per 100,000 population (RT). All 36 expected cells are present (no missing values). This satisfies need N6 (national yearly context on PM2.5-attributable deaths) for both prototype and production windows.

documentation_excerpts: This indicator estimates the number of premature deaths attributable to long-term exposure to PM2.5.

PM2.5 are particulates whose diameter is less than 2.5 micrometres and which can be carried deep into the lungs where they can cause inflammation and exacerbate the condition of people suffering from heart or lung diseases.
Dataset SDG_11_52, version 1.0, data structure SDG_11_52 v10.0
quality_notes: Year 2006 is absent from the time dimension (18 years listed: 2005, 2007–2023). Gap is documented in the data.
Only Italy (national) – no sub-national or NUTS-level breakdowns.
No status flags on any values (status_counts is empty), suggesting all values are normal estimates without provisional or confidential markers.
The data is annual only – hourly/daily resolution not available, which is appropriate for the 'national yearly context' need (N6).

Licence URL could not be reached via probe_url (EU Login redirect). However, Eurostat's publicly available data is under the Commission's reuse decision (2011/833/EU), which permits commercial reuse with attribution.
